regions.literal: Iesu saluator seculi / redemptis ope subueni [...]
regions.body: A notated I-initial hymn opening is followed by redemptis ope subueni and further continuous verse text. The local literal reading is provisional; no exact complete hymn edition or distinctive shared variant is established.

A notated I-initial opening reads Iesu redemptor seculi, followed by an uncertain continuation and continuous verse text. It resembles10349 in subject/opening words but is not securely the same complete work or a diagnostic variant.

A blue A-initial notated opening is followed by continuous verse lines. This is compatible with the catalogue A patre unigenitus cue; complete text/work/service identification and book identity remain separate.

Viewed upright by an exact180-degree rotation, the source has a notated hymn opening followed by continuous verse-like text in a narrow writing field. The rotation adds no source detail or original-side assignment.
The visible Off. and Secreta rubrics occur with notated chant and a prose prayer. This supports local Mass context already described by the published Beauvais record, not a newly identified book.

regions.literal: [...] galilei quid admiramini / aspicientes in celum [...]
regions.body: The right-hand music field includes the Galilei/aspicientes-in-celum passage. Its published Beauvais reconstruction membership remains credited separately; a liturgical phrase is not a unique codex fingerprint.
A red off.-like rubric precedes an Exultabunt sancti candidate opening in a broad notated field. This is a selected local genre/work cue, not a complete gradual classification or a book exclusion.

The preserved Advent-like passage occupies one broad music/text field. No central narrow-column gutter is visible within it. This differs from10349 copying-field design, without excluding section changes or composite volumes.
The surviving music/text uses one broad writing field, with its right extent cropped. Cropping is not treated as a narrow-column gutter or a complete original leaf/fold map.

limits: 15 retained photo views cover nine existing objects. Six objects have only one of their source views retained in this protocol; no complete canvas or medieval-side coverage is claimed.
General two-column appearance, square notation, different feasts and different book-section genres cannot by themselves establish or exclude a historical codex.
Exact complete hymn/music correspondence, a unique address or physical join is not established. No exhaustive chant census or independent source reading is claimed.
Literal source candidates precede reference lookup; a modern catalogue/reference must not fill difficult source letters silently.
